coverage.headline: OpenAI Loses Privacy Gambit: 20 Million ChatGPT Logs Likely Headed to Copyright Plaintiffs
coverage.summary: Judge Sidney Stein — who also oversees the Britannica case — compelled OpenAI to produce 20 million anonymized ChatGPT logs to plaintiffs in the consolidated MDL (In re: OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation), a discovery ruling with direct implications for the stayed Britannica action.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: April 7, 2026
coverage.summary: McKool Smith's litigation update reported that the court issued a show cause order to Encyclopaedia Britannica asking why its case should not be stayed pending summary judgment in the other active MDL cases, with a response deadline of April 15, 2026. The update noted it was likely the Britannica case would be stayed, as it had not been especially active in MDL filings.

coverage.headline: The dictionaries are suing OpenAI for 'massive' copyright infringement, and say ChatGPT is starving publishers of revenue
coverage.summary: Fortune reported that Britannica and Merriam-Webster filed suit in the Southern District of New York, alleging OpenAI built its business on their researched content and that ChatGPT cannibalizes the traffic and ad revenue publishers depend on. The suit also accuses OpenAI of feeding its LLM with the fact-checked work of hundreds of human writers and editors.

coverage.headline: Encyclopedia Britannica sues OpenAI over AI training
coverage.summary: The Maryland Daily Record reported that Britannica's lawsuit accuses OpenAI of unlawfully copying nearly 100,000 of its articles to train GPT large language models, with OpenAI responding that its models are 'grounded in fair use.' The piece situates the case within the broader wave of high-stakes copyright lawsuits by publishers and authors against AI companies.

coverage.headline: OpenAI sued by Merriam-Webster for copyright infringement
coverage.summary: Reports that the lawsuit alleges OpenAI's retrieval-augmented generation system pulls from Britannica's content in real time, and that trademark claims center on ChatGPT presenting invented content under Britannica's name. OpenAI responded that its models are 'grounded in fair use.'

coverage.headline: Encyclopedia Britannica, Merriam-Webster sue OpenAI over 'Massive Copyright' Infringement
coverage.summary: The Washington Times reported that the complaint alleges OpenAI scraped nearly 100,000 Britannica encyclopedia entries and Merriam-Webster dictionary definitions without authorization, and that ChatGPT generates outputs containing full or near-verbatim reproductions, diverting users and depriving the publishers of subscription and advertising revenue.

coverage.headline: Britannica, Merriam-Webster Accuse OpenAI of Copying Their Works
coverage.summary: Bloomberg Law reports that Encyclopaedia Britannica and Merriam-Webster filed suit against OpenAI in the S.D.N.Y. (No. 1:26-cv-02097) alleging massive copyright infringement, including copying the dictionary's own definition of 'plagiarize,' and trademark infringement when ChatGPT hallucinates false information attributed to the publishers. Both complaints were filed by Susman Godfrey LLP, which also represents news organizations in other AI copyright suits.
